content.value_statement: Frontend teams often repeat component, state, and performance decisions without a shared reference. This skill provides concise React and Next.js patterns that guide consistent implementation.
actual_capabilities: Provides React composition, compound component, and render prop examples.
Shows custom hooks for toggles, async fetching, and debounced input.
Demonstrates context and reducer state management for shared UI state.
Covers memoization, lazy loading, and list virtualization patterns.
Includes form validation, error boundaries, animation, keyboard navigation, and focus management.
limitations: It does not execute, test, or verify generated frontend code.
Examples are TypeScript snippets and may need project-specific changes.
It does not cover backend API design or deployment configuration.
Some examples use simplified placeholder components and sample data.

use_cases.title: Standardize React Components
use_cases.description: Use composition and compound component examples to create predictable component APIs across a product.

use_cases.title: Improve Interface Performance
use_cases.description: Apply memoization, lazy loading, and virtualization patterns to reduce slow renders in complex screens.

use_cases.title: Review UI Accessibility Patterns
use_cases.description: Use keyboard navigation and focus management examples when designing modals, dropdowns, and interactive controls.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a frontend pattern from this skill for [problem]. Explain when to use it and what tradeoffs to check.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the composition and compound component patterns to design [component]. Keep the API simple and list required props.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React view for memoization, lazy loading, and virtualization opportunities. Suggest specific changes using the skill patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Frontend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a frontend plan for [feature] using component composition, custom hooks, context reducers, forms, error handling, animation, and accessibility patterns.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable tab interface for a dashboard.
output_examples.output: Recommends the compound component pattern, defines the main responsibilities, and explains how shared state should flow through context.

output_examples.input: My market list has thousands of rows and scrolls slowly.
output_examples.output: Suggests virtualization, stable row heights, overscan, and memoized item components to reduce rendering work.

output_examples.input: I need an accessible modal pattern.
output_examples.output: Combines animation, focus management, Escape handling, and dialog attributes into a concise implementation checklist.

best_practices: Choose patterns that match the feature complexity and team maintenance needs.
Keep reusable component APIs small, typed, and consistent across similar components.
Pair performance changes with measurement before and after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not add context or reducers for local state that only one component owns.
Do not memoize every value without a clear render cost or stability need.
Do not copy examples without adapting accessibility behavior to the final UI.

faq.question: Does this skill run frontend code?
faq.answer: No. It provides written React and TypeScript examples for an assistant to adapt.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns are useful for React and Next.js interfaces, but routing details are not covered.

faq.question: Does it include state management guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes custom hooks, context, and reducer examples for shared UI state.

faq.question: Can it improve performance?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for memoization, lazy loading, and virtualization. You should still measure real application behavior.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes keyboard navigation and focus management examples for interactive components.

faq.question: Is it a complete design system?
faq.answer: No. It is a pattern reference, not a full component library or visual design system.
